title: Functional analyses for site-specific phosphorylation of a target protein in cells
protocol: Emulsify adjuvant with antigen using option A and/or option B before immunization.
Mix Freund complete adjuvant well and load a syringe with 0.5 ml per rabbit.
Dilute phosphopeptide-conjugated KLH in PBS to contain 0.2-0.4 mg/ml phosphopeptide.
Load another syringe with 0.5 ml antigen solution containing 0.1-0.2 mg phosphopeptide per rabbit.
Connect the two syringes via an 18 gauge double emulsifying needle.
Mix adjuvant and antigen by forcing materials back and forth through the needle.
Push all of the emulsion into one syringe and disconnect the empty syringe.
Warm RIBI adjuvant vial to 40-45°C for 5-10 minutes.
Dilute phosphopeptide-conjugated KLH with PBS to make a solution containing 0.1-0.2 mg/ml phosphopeptide.
Inject 2 ml of antigen solution per 2 rabbits directly into the vial through the rubber stopper using a syringe with a 21 gauge needle.
Vortex the vial while leaving the cap seal and rubber stopper in place.
Load a syringe with 1 ml emulsion corresponding to 0.1-0.2 mg phosphopeptide per rabbit.
Store unused adjuvant/antigen emulsion at 4°C for several months if the antigen is stable.
Collect blood from each rabbit before immunization to obtain preimmune serum (0.5-1 ml).
Immunize a rabbit by injecting 1 ml of prepared adjuvant/antigen emulsion corresponding to 0.1-0.2 mg phosphopeptide.
For Freund adjuvant system, inject the emulsion at multiple intradermal sites.
For RIBI adjuvant system, inject 0.05 ml per site × 6 intradermal, 0.3 ml intramuscular into each hind leg (total 2 sites), and 0.1 ml subcutaneous in neck region.
Perform booster injections every 4 weeks.
Incubate blood from each rabbit at 37°C for 1 hour.
Stir the incubated blood at 4°C overnight.
Centrifuge each sample at 1,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant (serum) from each centrifuged sample.
Incubate serum at 56°C for 30 minutes to inactivate complement system (optional).
Filtrate each serum sample through a 0.22 μm filter.
Check antibody titer against phosphopeptide using ELISA (optional).
Store aliquots of the serum samples at -80°C.
Prepare one 15 ml tube for each peptide.
Swell 0.2 mg TSKgel AF-Tresyl Toyopal650 with 1 ml coupling buffer in each tube.
Spin down the gel matrix and remove supernatant.
Dissolve 1 mg phosphorylated or non-phosphorylated peptide with 1 ml coupling buffer.
Check pH of the solution, which must be between 8.0-9.0.
Mix each peptide solution with 1 ml swollen matrix in a 15 ml tube.
Rotate gently for 4 hours at room temperature or overnight at 4°C on a rotor.
Spin down the gel matrix and remove peptide solution.
Wash gel matrix with 10 gel volumes (10 ml) of blocking buffer.
Add 10 gel volumes (10 ml) of blocking buffer to tube.
Rotate additionally for 1-2 hours at room temperature or for 4 hours at 4°C.
Spin down the gel matrix and remove the blocking buffer.
Equilibrate the gel matrix with TBS for short-term storage or the stock solution for long-term storage.
Store at 4 °C.
Dilute the serum with an equal volume of TBS (optional).
Mix the diluted serum with 1 ml of non-phosphorylated peptide-coupled gel matrix in a suitable tube.
Rotate the mixture end-over-end overnight to attach antibodies against non-phosphorylated peptide to the matrix.
Load the mixture onto a suitable column.
Collect the flow-through.
Wash the column with 1 ml of TBS and collect the flow-through, repeating this step 2-3 times.
Mix all flow-through fractions and keep them at 4 °C.
Wash the column with excess elution buffer (over 10 bed volumes).
Equilibrate with stock solution for long-term storage or TBS for immediate re-use after washing.
Check pH of the final flow-through fraction, which must be around 7.5.
Repeat steps 17-21 (optional).
Mix all flow-through fractions with 1 ml of the phosphopeptide-coupled gel matrix in a suitable tube.
Rotate the mixture end-over-end overnight.
Load the mixture onto a suitable column.
Wash the column with 10 bed volumes of TBS, twice.
Wash the column with 10 bed volumes of wash buffer, twice.
Wash the column with 10 bed volumes of TBS, twice.
Prepare 40 μl of neutralizing buffer in each collecting tube.
Mix 0.5 ml elution buffer with 40 μl of neutralizing buffer and check the pH, which must be around 7.5.
Elute the antibody with half bed volume of elution buffer using a stepwise elution.
Collect each drop of elute into the tube prepared above.
Mix immediately but gently in the tube.
Repeat the elution 5-6 times.
Apply 5-10 μl per elute to sodium dodecylsulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE).
Check its amount and purity of IgG, which can be detected as bands corresponding to 50-55 kDa and 20-55 kDa.
Collect the antibody-rich fractions (likely 2-3 fractions).
Add about 0.05 volume of 20 mg/ml BSA to the antibody solution.
Dialyze the antibody solution for 3-6 hours with 200 ml TBS, exchanging TBS at least once during dialysis.
Aliquot and immediately freeze the antibody solution in liquid nitrogen after dialysis.
Store the aliquoted antibody solution at -80°C.
Use 200 ml TBS containing 50% (v/v) glycerol as a dialyzing buffer for concentrating the antibody solution by centrifugation.
Store the concentrated antibody solution at -20°C after dialysis.
Design PCR primers to amplify the coding sequence of the gene.
Mix 35 μl of sterile water, 5 μl of 10 x KOD plus buffer, 2 μl of 25 mM MgSO4, 5 μl of 2 mM dNTPs mix, 1 μl (100 ng) of template DNA, 0.5 μl each of 10 μM primers and 1 μl (1 unit) of KOD plus.
Subject the mixture to PCR cycles consisting of 1 cycle at 98°C for 1 min followed by 10 cycles of 98°C for 5 sec, 50°C for 10 sec, and 68°C for 1 min per kb of product size.

Transfer 10 μl of the reaction to a PCR reaction mixture consisting of 21.6 μl sterile water, 10 μl of 10x KOD buffer, 1.6 μl of 25 mM MgSO4, 4 μl of 2 mM dNTPs mix, and 4 μl each of attB adaptor primers.
Add 0.8 μl (0.8 unit) of KOD plus to the PCR reaction mixture.
Subject the mixture to a cycle of 98°C for 1 minute, followed by 5 cycles of 98°C for 5 seconds, 45°C for 10 seconds, and 68°C for 1 minute per kb of product size.
Continue with 15 cycles of 98°C for 5 seconds, 50°C for 10 seconds, and 68°C for 1 minute per kb of product size.
Apply 5 μl of the PCR products to a 0.9% agarose gel electrophoresis.
If the template DNA is kanamycin-resistant plasmid, add 5 μl of 10x DpnI reaction buffer and 5 units of DpnI to the PCR product.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Heat inactivate the DpnI by incubating at 65°C for 15 minutes.
Add 150 μl of TE buffer and 100 μl of 30% PEG8000/30 mM MgCl2 to the PCR product.
Vortex well and centrifuge at 15,000rpm for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant from the mixture.
Dissolve the pellet in 20 μl of TE buffer.
Mix 1 μl of 5x BP reaction buffer, 2.5 μl of PCR products, 0.5 μl (75 ng) of pDONR221 and 1 μl of BP clonase.
Incubate at 25°C for 60 min.
Add 0.5 μl of proteinase K solution, and incubate for 10 min at 37°C.
Transform 50 μl of DH10b chemical competent cells with 2 μl of the BP reaction.
Select colonies on LB plate containing 30 μg ml^-1^ kanamycin.
Pick up colonies, and check the insert size of the plasmids.
Check the cloned gene by sequencing with M13 forward and reverse primers and oligonucleotides designed to cover the whole gene.
Mix 1 μl of 5x LR reaction buffer, 1.5 μl (50-100 ng) entry plasmid DNA, 1.5 μl of pDEST-CMSCVpuro (50-100 ng) and 1 μl of LR clonase enzyme mix.
Incubate at 25°C for 60 min to overnight.
Add 0.5 μl of proteinase K solution to stop the reaction.
Transform 50 μl of DH10b chemical competent cells with 2 μl of the LR reaction.
Select colonies on LB plate containing 100 μg ml^-1^ ampicillin.
Check the cloned gene by cutting with BsrG1 which cuts recombination sites (attB) of the reaction.
Seed 293T or 293FT cells at a density of 3.0 × 10^5 cells per 90-mm dish and cultivate them in a CO₂ incubator at 37 °C for 24 h.
Add 30 ml of TransIT293 to 500 ml of D-MEM without serum and mix well by vortex mixer.
Stand the mixture for 5 min.
Add 5 μg of the retroviral vector plasmid (i.e., pCMSCVpuro-mINCENP-HA) and 5 μg of pCL-10A1 to the solution and mix well by vortex mixer.
Stand the mixture for 10 min.
Add the solution onto the cells in a dish and incubate the cells at 37 °C for 36 h.
Aspirate the medium and add 10 ml of fresh growth medium with care not to detach cells, and incubate the cells at 37 °C for additional 24 h.
Collect the medium with a 10 ml syringe.
Filter the collected medium through a 0.45 μm-disk filter.
Aliquot the filtered medium (viral fluid) in screw capped tubes.
Freeze and store the tubes at -80 °C.
Seed HeLa cells at a density of 5 × 10^4 cells per well in a 12-well plate and cultivate them in a CO₂ incubator at 37 °C for 24 h.
Aspirate the medium and add 1 ml of growth medium supplemented with 8 μg/ml of polybrene to each well.
Dilute the viral stock 100 times with growth medium supplemented with 8 μg/ml of polybrene.
Add 0, 1, 10 and 100 μl of diluted viral fluid to each well in a row.
Incubate the cells at 37°C for an additional 24 hours.
Aspirate the medium from the wells.
Add growth medium to the wells and incubate at 37°C for an additional 24 hours.
Aspirate the medium from the wells.
Add 2 ml of growth medium supplemented with 0.5 μg/ml puromycin per well.
Change the medium, supplemented with 0.5 mg/ml puromycin, every fourth day.
Fix the cells with methanol.
Stain the cells with a 25-fold diluted Giemsa staining solution.
Count the number of colonies in each well.
Calculate the titer (drug-resistant colony-forming units per ml) for each virus.
If twenty colonies are observed in a well infected with 10 μl of a 100-fold diluted viral fluid, calculate the titer as 20 × 10,000 = 2.0 × 10^5 cfu/ml.
Seed HeLa cells at a density of 1 x 10^5 cells per well in a 6-well plate.
Cultivate the seeded cells in a CO2 incubator at 37°C for 24 h.
Thaw the frozen viral fluid in a metal tube stand or water bath at room temperature.
Take approximately 10^5 cfu of each viral fluid and add 2 mg/ml of polybrene to achieve an 8 mg/ml final concentration.
Aspirate the medium from the cells.
Add growth medium supplemented with 8 mg/ml of polybrene to the cells.
Add the viral fluid to each well containing the seeded HeLa cells.
Incubate the cells at 37°C for an additional 24 h.
Include plain-vector virus-infected cells and mock-infected cells as controls.
Aspirate the medium from the infected cells.
Add growth medium to the infected cells.
Incubate the cells at 37°C for an additional 24 h.
Aspirate the medium from the cells.
Add growth medium supplemented with 0.5 mg/ml puromycin to the cells.
Change the medium supplemented with 0.5 μg/ml puromycin every three days until all mock-infected HeLa cells die, usually taking 3 to 5 days.
If the cells reach confluence, trypsinize the cells and transfer them into a 90-mm dish for further selection and propagation.
The pooled population can be used generally for further experiments.
If necessary, clone the infected cells by limiting dilution and examine individual clones.
Plate HeLa cells in growth medium one day before transfection.
Incubate the cells at 37°C in a CO₂ incubator for approximately 24 hours.
Dilute 10 μl of 20 μM annealed oligos in 170 μl of Opti-MEM without serum and antibiotics.
Mix gently.
Dilute 2-4 μl of Oligofectamine in 15 μl of Opti-MEM medium without serum and antibiotics.
Mix gently.
Incubate the diluted Oligofectamine at room temperature for 5-10 minutes.
Combine the diluted siRNA with the diluted Oligofectamine; total volume is about 0.2 ml.
Mix gently.
Incubate the combined solution at room temperature for 15-20 minutes.
Wash cells twice with 2 ml of Opti-MEM.
Add 0.8 ml of Opti-MEM to each dish.
Combine siRNA:Oligofectamine complexes and add them to each dish; total volume is approximately 1 ml.
Mix gently by rocking the plate back and forth.
Incubate the cells at 37°C in a CO₂ incubator for 4 hours.
Incubate the cells for 4 hours.
Add 1 ml of DMEM supplemented with 20% FBS to achieve a final FBS concentration of about 10%.
Mix gently by rocking the plate back and forth.
Incubate the cells at 37°C in a CO₂ incubator.
Use the cells for immunocytochemistry, immunoblotting, etc., at 24-72 hours after addition of siRNA oligo.
